# package uasc

```go
import "github.com/otfabric/go-opcua/uasc"
```

Package uasc provides encoding/decoding and automated secure channel and session handling for OPC UA Secure Conversation.

```go
const (
	// SchemeHTTPS is the URL scheme of HTTPS endpoints (Part 6 §7.4.1). The
	// transport underneath is plain https.
	SchemeHTTPS = "opc.https"

	// HTTPSContentType is the Content-Type of UA Binary messages over
	// HTTPS (Part 6 §7.4.4).
	HTTPSContentType = "application/octet-stream"

	// HTTPSContentTypeLegacy is the Content-Type of UA Binary messages that
	// older applications use; it is accepted for backward compatibility
	// (Part 6 §7.4.2).
	HTTPSContentTypeLegacy = "application/opcua+uabinary"

	// HTTPSSecurityPolicyHeader is the HTTP header that names the security
	// policy of the client (Part 6 §7.4.1). Without it the server assumes
	// None.
	HTTPSSecurityPolicyHeader = "OPCUA-SecurityPolicy"

	// MaxHTTPSMessageSize is the size limit of an HTTPS response body a
	// client accepts.
	MaxHTTPSMessageSize = 16 << 20
)
```

The HTTPS transport with UA Binary encoding (Part 6 §7.4, profile https-uabinary) has no secure conversation: each request is the body of an HTTP POST and its response the body of the HTTP response, encoded as the encoding NodeId of the service structure followed by the structure. TLS protects the messages. The SecurityPolicy of the endpoint, named in the OPCUA-SecurityPolicy header, only decides how the nonces of CreateSession and ActivateSession are signed (Part 6 §7.4.1); with None they are not.

```go
const (
	// HTTPSJSONContentType is the Content-Type of JSON messages over HTTPS
	// (Part 6 §7.4.5).
	HTTPSJSONContentType = "application/json"

	// HTTPSJSONContentTypeLegacy is the Content-Type of JSON messages over
	// HTTPS that UA-.NETStandard uses. A server accepts it next to
	// HTTPSJSONContentType and answers with the Content-Type of the request.
	HTTPSJSONContentTypeLegacy = "application/opcua+uajson"

	// MaxWebSocketJSONMessageSize is the size limit of a JSON message a
	// client receives over a WebSocket; a larger one ends the connection
	// with status 1009 (Part 6 §7.5.2).
	MaxWebSocketJSONMessageSize = MaxHTTPSMessageSize

	// maxIdleWebSockets is the number of idle WebSockets a wss-uajson
	// channel keeps for the next requests.

	// webSocketIdleTimeout is how long a wss-uajson channel keeps an idle
	// WebSocket. It is shorter than the time a server waits for the next
	// request, so that a request is not sent on a WebSocket the server is
	// closing.

)
```

The UA JSON mappings of HTTPS and WebSockets (transport profiles https-uajson and wss-uajson) have no secure conversation either. A service request or response is a JSON message: "Messages are encoded as ExtensionObjects" (Part 6 §5.4.9), which in the JSON encoding of OPC UA 1.05 is a JSON object with the UaTypeId of the DataType of the message followed by the fields of the structure (Part 6 §5.4.2.16). The messages are written in the compact form (Part 6 §7.4.2, Table 80: application/json is "OPC UA JSON Compact"); the verbose form and the 1.04 form are accepted as well. Over HTTPS each message is the body of an HTTP POST or response with the Content-Type application/json (Part 6 §7.4.5). Over a WebSocket with the sub-protocol opcua+uajson each message is one WebSocket message (Part 6 §7.5.2).

Without a secure conversation the security policy can only matter for the session signatures. HTTPS names it in the OPCUA-SecurityPolicy header; a WebSocket has no such header, so wss-uajson endpoints use the policy None and TLS alone protects the messages.

## Functions

### func DecodeServiceMessageJSON

```go
func DecodeServiceMessageJSON(b []byte, namespaces []string) (any, error)
```

DecodeServiceMessageJSON decodes a JSON message (Part 6 §5.4.9) into the service request or response it holds. It accepts the compact and verbose forms of OPC UA 1.05 and the form of 1.04. namespaces is the NamespaceArray the namespace URIs of NodeIds are looked up in. The errors wrap ua.StatusBadDecodingError, or ua.StatusBadServiceUnsupported for a message that is not a service request or response.

The compact form leaves out the fields that have their default value, and a decoded message has no value for them: a structure or a NodeId that was left out is nil. The message is therefore completed the way the UA Binary decoder fills in every field, by passing it through UA Binary, so that the services see the same message whatever the encoding.

### func DecryptUserSecret

```go
func DecryptUserSecret(key *uapolicy.EphemeralKey, data, signerCertificate, nonce []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

DecryptUserSecret verifies and decrypts an EccEncryptedSecret a client created for the ephemeral key. The secret must be signed with the key of signerCertificate, the client's application instance certificate, and be bound to nonce, the session nonce the server issued last.

### func HTTPSPolicySupported

```go

```

HTTPSPolicySupported reports whether a security policy can be used over HTTPS. A policy that binds the session to the ChannelThumbprint of a secure conversation (Part 6 §6.7.5, the policies with SecureChannelEnhancements) cannot: HTTPS has no secure conversation and so no thumbprint.

### func NewHTTPSClient

```go
func NewHTTPSClient(tlsConfig *tls.Config) *http.Client
```

NewHTTPSClient returns the HTTP client of the HTTPS transport: HTTP/1.1 (Part 6 §7.4.4) over TLS 1.2 or later with tlsConfig, nil for the system roots. There is no overall request timeout: every request is bounded by the timeout of the service call, and a Publish request is held by the server until it has something to send.

```go
type Config struct {

	// SecurityPolicyURI is the URI of the Security Policy used to secure the Message.
	// This field is encoded as a UTF-8 string without a null terminator.
	SecurityPolicyURI string

	// Certificate is the X.509 v3 Certificate assigned to the sending application Instance.
	// This is a DER encoded blob.
	// The structure of an X.509 v3 Certificate is defined in X.509 v3.
	// The DER format for a Certificate is defined in X690.
	// This indicates what Private Key was used to sign the MessageChunk.
	// The Stack shall close the channel and report an error to the application if
	// the Certificate is too large for the buffer size supported by the
	// transport layer.
	// This field shall be null if the Message is not signed.
	Certificate []byte

	// LocalKey is a RSA Private Key which will be used to encrypt the OpenSecureChannel
	// messages.  It is the key associated with Certificate
	//
	// For a key of another type (the ECC security policies) set
	// LocalPrivateKey instead.
	LocalKey *rsa.PrivateKey

	// LocalPrivateKey is the private key associated with Certificate, of any
	// supported type: an *rsa.PrivateKey for the RSA security policies, a
	// crypto.Signer with an ECDSA public key for the ECC ones. It takes
	// precedence over LocalKey.
	LocalPrivateKey crypto.Signer

	// UserKey is a RSA Private Key which will be used to sign the UserTokenSignature.
	// It is the key associated with AuthCertificate
	//
	// For a key of another type set UserPrivateKey instead.
	UserKey *rsa.PrivateKey

	// UserPrivateKey is the private key associated with the certificate of an
	// X509IdentityToken, of any supported type. It takes precedence over
	// UserKey.
	UserPrivateKey crypto.Signer

	// LocalIdentity, when set on a server SecureChannel, selects the
	// application instance certificate and private key for the security
	// policy a client opens the channel with. A server that offers RSA and
	// ECC endpoints has one certificate per key type; the policy decides
	// which one applies. It is called once, for the first OpenSecureChannel
	// request, and its result replaces Certificate and LocalPrivateKey.
	// An error rejects the channel with Bad_SecurityPolicyRejected.
	LocalIdentity func(securityPolicyURI string) (certificate []byte, key crypto.Signer, err error)

	// Thumbprint is the thumbprint of the X.509 v3 Certificate assigned to the receiving
	// application Instance.
	// The thumbprint is the CertificateDigest of the DER encoded form of the
	// Certificate.
	// This indicates what public key was used to encrypt the MessageChunk.
	// This field shall be null if the Message is not encrypted.
	Thumbprint []byte

	// RemoteCertificate is the X.509 Certificate for the receiving instance.
	// Used to encrypt the message chunks in the OpenSecureChannel phase.
	RemoteCertificate []byte

	// RequestIDSeed is the initial value for RequestID counter in each new SecureChannel
	RequestIDSeed uint32

	// SecurityMode is The type of security to apply to the messages. The type MessageSecurityMode
	// is defined in 7.15.
	// A SecureChannel may have to be created even if the securityMode is NONE. The exact behaviour
	// depends on the mapping used and is described in the Part 6.
	SecurityMode ua.MessageSecurityMode

	// AutoReconnect will make sure that once communication is restored,
	// the old session is used whenever possible and that Susbcription data is not missed.
	// You may choose to use AutoReconnect (true by default) or do it manually.
	// AutoReconnect will make the UaClient to try to reconnect to the server every second,
	// once the communication is broken. If you do it manually, you must be prepared to do it until it succeeds.
	AutoReconnect bool

	// ReconnectInterval is interval duration between each reconnection attempt,
	// ignored if AutoReconnect is set to false.
	ReconnectInterval time.Duration

	// Lifetime is the requested lifetime, in milliseconds, for the new SecurityToken when the
	// SecureChannel works as client. It specifies when the Client expects to renew the SecureChannel
	// by calling the OpenSecureChannel Service again. If a SecureChannel is not renewed, then all
	// Messages sent using the current SecurityTokens shall be rejected by the receiver.
	// Lifetime can also be the revised lifetime, the lifetime of the SecurityToken in milliseconds.
	// The UTC expiration time for the token may be calculated by adding the lifetime to the createdAt time.
	Lifetime uint32

	// RequestTimeout is timeout duration for all synchronous requests over SecureChannel.
	// If the Server doesn't respond within RequestTimeout time, Client returns StatusBadTimeout
	RequestTimeout time.Duration

	// Logger is the logger for protocol-level messages.
	// If nil, logging is disabled.
	Logger *slog.Logger

	// ClientCertificateValidator, when set on a server SecureChannel, is
	// invoked during OpenSecureChannel after the peer certificate is known.
	// Return nil to accept; return a ua.StatusCode (typically
	// StatusBadCertificateUntrusted) to reject the channel open.
	// Nil means no application-certificate trust check at channel open.
	ClientCertificateValidator func(certDER []byte) error

	// OpenSecureChannelHook, when set on a server SecureChannel, is called
	// for every OpenSecureChannel request the channel handled, issue or
	// renewal, with the status it was answered with: StatusOK once the
	// response has been sent, the error otherwise. A request the channel
	// cannot decrypt or verify is not seen. The hook runs on the goroutine
	// that reads the channel and must not block.
	OpenSecureChannelHook func(req *ua.OpenSecureChannelRequest, status ua.StatusCode)

	// HTTPSJSONContentType is the Content-Type of the requests of an
	// https-uajson channel (NewHTTPSJSONChannel). Empty means
	// HTTPSJSONContentType (Part 6 §7.4.2); HTTPSJSONContentTypeLegacy
	// reaches servers that take only that one (UA-.NETStandard 2.0.1).
	HTTPSJSONContentType string
}
```

### type SecureChannel

```go
type SecureChannel struct {

	// c is the uacp connection

	// cfg is the configuration for the secure channel.

	// time returns the current time. When not set it defaults to time.Now().

	// closing is channel used to indicate to go routines that the secure channel is closing

	// startDispatcher ensures only one dispatcher is running

	// requestID is a "global" counter shared between multiple channels and tokens

	// instances maps secure channel IDs to a list to channel states

	// maxLifetime is the longest SecurityToken lifetime (ms) a server channel
	// grants; captured from the configured lifetime on the first open.

	// renewing is set on a server channel while a renewal that was received
	// in full is being processed, and expiryDeferred holds the token whose
	// lifetime ran out meanwhile; see scheduleServerTokenExpiry. Both are
	// guarded by instancesMu.

	// sendGate keeps requests and token renewal apart: every request holds
	// the read side while it is written to the connection and a renewal
	// holds the write side. A renewal therefore starts only when no request
	// is half-way out, and no request picks a channel instance while the
	// token is being replaced.

	// openWaitCh is closed by the open() call that sent request openWaitID
	// when it returns. The dispatcher waits for it after forwarding the
	// OpenSecureChannelResponse to that request, so that no new messages
	// are read while the channel's crypto state is being updated. It is
	// nil while no open() is waiting for a response.
	//
	// The wait belongs to one request: an open() that ended without a
	// response (timeout, cancellation) must not release the dispatcher
	// early when the response of a later open() arrives.

	// handlers maps request ids to the requests waiting for their response

	// chunks maintains a temporary list of chunks for a given request ID

	// chunkBytes is the number of body bytes in chunks for a request ID, so
	// that a message larger than MaxMessageSize is refused while its chunks
	// arrive rather than after all of them have been buffered. It is
	// guarded by chunksMu.

	// chunksAborted holds the request IDs whose collection was given up
	// (too many chunks or bytes): their remaining chunks are dropped up to
	// and including the final one, rather than collected again and merged
	// into a message of their own. It is guarded by chunksMu.

	// openingInstance is a temporary var that allows the dispatcher know how to handle a open channel request
	// note: we only allow a single "open" request in flight at any point in time. The mutex is held for the entire
	// duration of the "open" request.
	//
	// On a client open() sets and clears it while the dispatcher looks at
	// it for every OpenSecureChannel message it receives, solicited or
	// not: both go through opening() and setOpening().

	// errorCh receive dispatcher errors

	// required for the server channel

	// // secureChannelID is a unique identifier for the SecureChannel assigned by the Server.
	// // If a Server receives a SecureChannelId which it does not recognize it shall return an
	// // appropriate transport layer error.
	// //
	// // When a Server starts the first SecureChannelId used should be a value that is likely to
	// // be unique after each restart. This ensures that a Server restart does not cause
	// // previously connected Clients to accidentally ‘reuse’ SecureChannels that did not belong
	// // to them.
	// secureChannelID uint32

	// // sequenceNumber is a monotonically increasing sequence number assigned by the sender to each
	// // MessageChunk sent over the SecureChannel.
	// sequenceNumber uint32

	// // securityTokenID is a unique identifier for the SecureChannel SecurityToken used to secure the Message.
	// // This identifier is returned by the Server in an OpenSecureChannel response Message.
	// // If a Server receives a TokenId which it does not recognize it shall return an appropriate
	// // transport layer error.
	// securityTokenID uint32

	// kind indicates whether this is a server or a client channel.

	// peerCert is the certificate a client opened this (server) channel
	// with. It is kept apart from cfg so that it can be read while the
	// channel is in use.

	// lastReceivedSequenceNumber is the sequence number of the chunk that
	// was received last. The policies with authenticated encryption need it
	// to open the next chunk.

	// receivedAny is set once the first chunk has been received: from then
	// on the sequence numbers of a secured channel have to be contiguous.
	// Only the goroutine that reads the chunks uses it.

	// binding and keyChain are the state of the SecureChannelEnhancements
	// of OPC UA 1.05.07 (see channel_binding.go). keyChain is the key
	// material the next renewal is chained to; only the goroutine that
	// handles OpenSecureChannel messages uses it.

	// direct is the transport of a channel without UACP connection and
	// secure conversation: HTTPS (NewHTTPSChannel, NewHTTPSJSONChannel) or
	// WebSockets with JSON messages (NewWebSocketJSONChannel).

}
```

#### func NewCryptoChannel

```go
func NewCryptoChannel(cfg *Config) *SecureChannel
```

NewCryptoChannel returns a SecureChannel that can exercise the session and user-token cryptographic helpers without an underlying UACP connection. It must not be used for Open/SendRequest.

#### func NewHTTPSChannel

```go
func NewHTTPSChannel(endpoint string, httpClient *http.Client, cfg *Config, errCh chan<- error) (*SecureChannel, error)
```

NewHTTPSChannel returns a client channel to an opc.https (or https) endpoint. It has no connection of its own: Open does nothing and every request is posted with httpClient, NewHTTPSClient(nil) if nil. The session signatures use cfg like those of a secure conversation, and cfg's SecurityPolicyURI is sent in the OPCUA-SecurityPolicy header.

errCh receives the errors that ask for recovery, as for NewSecureChannel: a fault that invalidates the session, and the failure of a request to reach the server (wrapping io.EOF).

#### func NewWebSocketJSONChannel

```go
func NewWebSocketJSONChannel(endpoint string, dialer *uacp.Dialer, cfg *Config, errCh chan<- error) (*SecureChannel, error)
```

NewWebSocketJSONChannel returns a client channel to an opc.wss endpoint with the transport profile wss-uajson (Part 6 §7.5.2). There is no secure conversation: every request is a JSON message sent over a TLS secured WebSocket with the sub-protocol opcua+uajson, which dialer opens with its TLSConfig, and the next message on that WebSocket is the response. A WebSocket carries one request at a time, so a server that serves the requests of a WebSocket one after the other does not hold the others up behind a Publish request: the channel opens another WebSocket while all are busy, and keeps up to 8 idle ones for the next requests. Open does nothing, the WebSockets are opened when needed.

cfg must have the security policy None and the mode None: unlike HTTPS a WebSocket cannot name a policy for the session signatures. errCh receives the errors that ask for recovery, as for NewHTTPSChannel.

#### func (SecureChannel) ChannelThumbprint

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) ChannelThumbprint() []byte
```

ChannelThumbprint returns the ChannelThumbprint of a SecureChannel whose security policy has SecureChannelEnhancements: the signature of the first OpenSecureChannel response. It is nil for every other channel and until the channel is open. The value identifies the channel to its two applications; it is not a secret.

#### func (SecureChannel) Close

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) Close() (err error)
```

Close closes an existing secure channel.

#### func (SecureChannel) Disconnected

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) Disconnected() <-chan struct{}
```

Disconnected returns a channel that is closed when the secure channel has stopped reading from its connection, because the connection was lost or the channel was closed. A client secure channel reports the loss of its connection only once on its error channel; Disconnected lets the owner check the current state at any later time.

For a channel that was never opened the returned channel is never closed.


EncryptUserSecret protects the secret of a user identity token (a password or the data of an issued token) for an ECC security policy. The result is an EccEncryptedSecret (Part 4 §7.41.2.3): encrypted with a key agreed with the ephemeral public key the server handed out and signed with the client's application instance key.

#### func (SecureChannel) LocalCertificate

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) LocalCertificate() []byte
```

LocalCertificate returns the application instance certificate this side of the channel uses. On a server with certificates of several key types it is the one selected for the security policy of the channel.

#### func (SecureChannel) LocalEndpoint

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) LocalEndpoint() string
```

#### func (SecureChannel) LocalPrivateKey

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) LocalPrivateKey() crypto.PrivateKey
```

LocalPrivateKey returns the private key of LocalCertificate, or nil if there is none.

#### func (SecureChannel) NewActivateSessionSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) NewActivateSessionSignature(serverCertificate, serverNonce, clientNonce []byte) ([]byte, string, error)
```

NewActivateSessionSignature creates the ClientSignature of an ActivateSession request (Part 4 §5.7.3, §6.1.8).

serverCertificate is the certificate of the CreateSession response, serverNonce the nonce the server issued last and clientNonce the nonce of the CreateSession request.

#### func (SecureChannel) NewCreateSessionSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) NewCreateSessionSignature(clientCertificate, clientNonce, serverNonce []byte) ([]byte, string, error)
```

NewCreateSessionSignature creates the ServerSignature of a CreateSession response (Part 4 §5.7.2, §6.1.8).

clientCertificate and clientNonce come from the request, serverNonce is the nonce of the response. On a channel with SecureChannelEnhancements the signature is bound to the channel; otherwise it covers the client certificate and the client nonce.

#### func (SecureChannel) NewEphemeralKeySignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) NewEphemeralKeySignature(policyURI string, publicKey []byte) ([]byte, error)
```

NewEphemeralKeySignature signs an ephemeral public key with the local application instance key, as a server does for the EphemeralKeyType it returns from CreateSession and ActivateSession (Part 6 §6.8.2).

#### func (SecureChannel) NewSessionSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) NewSessionSignature(cert, nonce []byte) ([]byte, string, error)
```

NewSessionSignature issues a new signature for the client to send on the next ActivateSessionRequest.

#### func (SecureChannel) NewSessionUserTokenSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) NewSessionUserTokenSignature(policyURI string, serverCertificate, serverNonce, clientNonce []byte) ([]byte, string, error)
```

NewSessionUserTokenSignature creates the UserTokenSignature of an ActivateSession request for an X509IdentityToken, with the private key of the user certificate (Part 4 §6.1.8).

policyURI is the security policy of the UserTokenPolicy ("" selects the policy of the channel). The other arguments are those of NewActivateSessionSignature.

#### func (SecureChannel) NewUserTokenSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) NewUserTokenSignature(policyURI string, cert, nonce []byte) ([]byte, string, error)
```

NewUserTokenSignature issues a new signature for the client to send in ActivateSessionRequest The security policy for the SecureChannel is used if policyURI value is null or empty [https://reference.opcfoundation.org/Core/Part4/v104/docs/7.37](https://reference.opcfoundation.org/Core/Part4/v104/docs/7.37)

#### func (SecureChannel) Open

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) Open(ctx context.Context) error
```

#### func (SecureChannel) Receive

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) Receive(ctx context.Context) *MessageBody
```

Receive receives message chunks from the secure channel, decodes and forwards them to the registered callback channel, if there is one. Otherwise, the message is dropped.

#### func (SecureChannel) ReleaseTokens

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) ReleaseTokens()
```

ReleaseTokens stops the expiry timers of all SecurityTokens of the channel. A client channel does this when it is closed; for a server channel the channel broker calls it once the connection is gone. Either way a closed channel is not retained until its tokens would have expired.

#### func (SecureChannel) RemoteAddr

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) RemoteAddr() net.Addr
```

RemoteAddr returns the address of the peer, nil for a channel without a connection (an HTTPS or crypto-only channel).

#### func (SecureChannel) RemoteCertificate

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) RemoteCertificate() []byte
```

RemoteCertificate returns the DER encoded application instance certificate of the peer: on a server channel the certificate the client opened the channel with, on a client channel the configured server certificate. It is nil for a channel without security.

#### func (SecureChannel) Renew

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) Renew(ctx context.Context) error
```

#### func (SecureChannel) SecurityMode

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) SecurityMode() ua.MessageSecurityMode
```

SecurityMode returns the message security mode configured for this channel.

#### func (SecureChannel) SecurityPolicyURI

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) SecurityPolicyURI() string
```

SecurityPolicyURI returns the security policy URI configured for this channel.



#### func (SecureChannel) SetNamespaces

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) SetNamespaces(ns []string)
```

SetNamespaces sets the NamespaceArray of the server. The JSON encoding writes the NodeIds of namespaces other than 0 with their namespace URI and reads them back with it (Part 6 §5.4.2.10); without the array, or for an index it does not have, the namespace index is used. It has no effect on the other channels.

#### func (SecureChannel) UserTokenPolicyIsECC

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) UserTokenPolicyIsECC(policyURI string) bool
```

UserTokenPolicyIsECC reports whether the secrets of a user identity token with the given token security policy ("" selects the policy of the channel) are protected with an EccEncryptedSecret and an ephemeral key exchange.

#### func (SecureChannel) VerifyActivateSessionSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) VerifyActivateSessionSignature(clientCertificate, serverNonce, clientNonce, signature []byte) error
```

VerifyActivateSessionSignature checks the ClientSignature of an ActivateSession request. clientCertificate is the certificate the Session was created with.

#### func (SecureChannel) VerifyCreateSessionSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) VerifyCreateSessionSignature(serverCertificate, clientNonce, serverNonce, signature []byte) error
```

VerifyCreateSessionSignature checks the ServerSignature of a CreateSession response. serverCertificate, serverNonce and signature come from the response, clientNonce is the nonce of the request.

#### func (SecureChannel) VerifyEphemeralKeySignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) VerifyEphemeralKeySignature(policyURI string, certificate, publicKey, signature []byte) error
```

VerifyEphemeralKeySignature checks that an ephemeral public key was signed by the owner of the certificate.

#### func (SecureChannel) VerifySessionSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) VerifySessionSignature(cert, nonce, signature []byte) error
```

VerifySessionSignature checks the integrity of a Create/Activate Session response's signature.

#### func (SecureChannel) VerifySessionUserTokenSignature

```go
func (s *SecureChannel) VerifySessionUserTokenSignature(policyURI string, userCertificate, serverCertificate, serverNonce, clientNonce, signature []byte) error
```

VerifySessionUserTokenSignature checks the UserTokenSignature of an ActivateSession request against the certificate of the X509IdentityToken. serverCertificate is the application instance certificate the server returned from CreateSession.

### type SessionConfig

```go
type SessionConfig struct {
	// AuthenticationToken is the secret Session identifier used to verify that the request is
	// associated with the Session. The SessionAuthenticationToken type is defined in 7.31.
	AuthenticationToken *ua.NodeID

	// ClientDescription is the information that describes the Client application.
	// The type ApplicationDescription is defined in 7.1.
	ClientDescription *ua.ApplicationDescription

	// ServerEndpoints is the list of Endpoints that the Server supports.
	// The Server shall return a set of EndpointDescriptions available for the serverUri
	// specified in the request. The EndpointDescription type is defined in 7.10. The Client
	// shall verify this list with the list from a DiscoveryEndpoint if it used a
	// DiscoveryEndpoint to fetch the EndpointDescriptions.
	// It is recommended that Servers only include the server.applicationUri, endpointUrl,
	// securityMode, securityPolicyUri, userIdentityTokens, transportProfileUri and
	// securityLevel with all other parameters set to null. Only the recommended
	// parameters shall be verified by the client.
	ServerEndpoints []*ua.EndpointDescription

	// LocaleIDs is the list of locale ids in priority order for localized strings. The first
	// LocaleId in the list has the highest priority. If the Server returns a localized string
	// to the Client, the Server shall return the translation with the highest priority that
	// it can. If it does not have a translation for any of the locales identified in this list,
	// then it shall return the string value that it has and include the locale id with the
	// string. See Part 3 for more detail on locale ids. If the Client fails to specify at least
	// one locale id, the Server shall use any that it has.
	// This parameter only needs to be specified during the first call to ActivateSession during
	// a single application Session. If it is not specified the Server shall keep using the
	// current localeIds for the Session.
	LocaleIDs []string

	// UserIdentityToken is the credentials of the user associated with the Client application.
	// The Server uses these credentials to determine whether the Client should be allowed to
	// activate a Session and what resources the Client has access to during this Session.
	// The UserIdentityToken is an extensible parameter type defined in 7.36.
	// The EndpointDescription specifies what UserIdentityTokens the Server shall accept.
	// Null or empty user token shall always be interpreted as anonymous.
	UserIdentityToken ua.IdentityToken

	// If the Client specified a user identity token that supports digital signatures, then it
	// shall create a signature and pass it as this parameter. Otherwise the parameter is null.
	// The SignatureAlgorithm depends on the identity token type.
	// The SignatureData type is defined in 7.32.
	UserTokenSignature *ua.SignatureData

	// SessionName is an optional name of the session.
	// The default is a unique value for every new session.
	SessionName string

	// If Session works as a client, SessionTimeout is the requested maximum number of milliseconds
	// that a Session should remain open without activity. If the Client fails to issue a Service
	// request within this interval, then the Server shall automatically terminate the Client Session.
	// If Session works as a server, SessionTimeout is an actual maximum number of milliseconds
	// that a Session shall remain open without activity. The Server should attempt to honour the
	// Client request for this parameter,but may negotiate this value up or down to meet its own constraints.
	SessionTimeout time.Duration

	// Stored version of the password to authenticate against a server
	// todo: storing passwords in memory seems wrong
	AuthPassword string

	// PolicyURI to use when encrypting secrets for the User Identity Token
	// Could be different from the secure channel's policy
	AuthPolicyURI string

	// PendingPolicyID is set by AuthPolicyID when called before an AuthXXX
	// method. AuthXXX methods apply it after token creation so that
	// AuthPolicyID can be called in any order relative to AuthXXX.
	PendingPolicyID string
}
```

SessionConfig is a set of common configurations used in Session.
